findings.claim: The failure paths update retryCount with a read-modify-write assignment (`retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1`) after reading the row earlier in the job. If multiple cron/job workers process the same reminder concurrently, one worker can overwrite another worker's increment and undercount retries, which can prevent cleanup from triggering at the intended threshold.
findings.title: Retry counter updates can lose increments under concurrent cron workers

findings.claim: The initial `deleteMany` uses `OR: [{ method: SMS, scheduledDate <= now }, { retryCount: { gt: 1 } }]`, so any reminder of any method/domain with retryCount > 1 is deleted. This is not scoped to the SMS reminder flow and can remove unrelated reminders that happen to share the retryCount field.
findings.title: Cleanup deletes non-SMS reminders solely because retryCount is high
